items.followUp: Why does water have dipole-dipole forces of attraction?

rubric.why: HCl is polar because chlorine and hydrogen have different electronegativities.
rubric.description: Identifies HCl as a polar molecule due to an electronegativity difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HCl is polar or has a permanent dipole due to the electronegativity difference between H and Cl.

rubric.why: The positive end of one HCl molecule attracts the negative end of a neighbouring molecule.
rubric.description: Explains that opposite ends of neighbouring HCl molecules attract.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing attraction between opposite poles of neighbouring molecules.

modelAnswer: HCl is a polar molecule because chlorine and hydrogen have different electronegativities.
The positive end of one HCl molecule attracts the negative end of another, producing dipole-dipole forces.

items.followUp: Why does a solution form a homogeneous mixture?

rubric.why: Suspended particles are not distributed uniformly throughout the mixture.
rubric.description: States that suspension particles are not uniformly distributed, making the mixture heterogeneous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles are unevenly distributed or that a suspension is heterogeneous.

rubric.why: Suspension particles are large enough to settle out on standing.
rubric.description: States that suspension particles settle on standing or identifies their large size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles settle on standing or are large.

modelAnswer: The particles in a suspension are not uniformly distributed, so it is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its large particles settle down on standing.

items.followUp: Give two characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles scatter a beam of light.
rubric.description: States that colloids scatter light or show the Tyndall effect.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.
rubric.description: States that colloidal particles do not settle on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles remain suspended or do not settle.

modelAnswer: Colloidal particles scatter light and show the Tyndall effect.
They do not settle down on standing.

items.followUp: Define an aqueous solution of sodium chloride.

rubric.description: Identifies brine as a concentrated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as concentrated.

rubric.why: Brine is a solution of sodium chloride in water.
rubric.description: Identifies sodium chloride as the dissolved substance in brine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming sodium chloride.

modelAnswer: Brine is a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride (NaCl).

rubric.why: Sodium, potassium, lithium and cesium are very reactive metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

rubric.why: A second correct example is required.
rubric.description: Names a second very reactive metal different from the first.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct example.

modelAnswer: Sodium and potassium are two very reactive metals.

rubric.why: Silver is used to make jewellery, ornaments and coins.
rubric.description: Gives one use of silver in ornaments, jewellery or coins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid use.

rubric.why: Silver is also used in photography, mirrors and electrical applications.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid use of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct use.

modelAnswer: Silver is used for making jewellery and ornaments.
It is also used for making coins.

items.followUp: Write two physical properties of metals.

rubric.why: Non-metals commonly show physical properties such as brittleness, dullness and poor conductivity.
rubric.description: States one physical property of non-metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct physical property.

rubric.why: A second distinct physical property is required.
rubric.description: States a second physical property of non-metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct property.

modelAnswer: Non-metals are generally brittle in the solid state.
They are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
